claim: Fourlis' FY2025 annual report gives the price of FL's Greece/Romania sale to its licensee by country. Greece (3 stores plus footlocker.gr) went for EUR 9.498M against net assets of EUR 2.730M, so goodwill was EUR 6.768M (about 3.5x book). Romania (3 stores) went for EUR 2.114M against net assets of EUR 2.064M, so goodwill was EUR 50k (about book value). Greece was paid in full; for Romania only EUR 206k was paid and EUR 1.908M is deferred. After-tax results for Apr-Dec 2025 were +EUR 517k for Greece and -EUR 574k for Romania.
data_point: EUR 11.6M for 6 stores in total. Greece about EUR 3.2M per store (3.5x net assets); Romania about EUR 0.7M per store (book value). The Romanian stores lost money after the transfer.
source_name: Fourlis Holdings FY2025 Annual Financial Report (ATHEX iXBRL), pp.416-417
original_quote: The transaction amount totaled €9,498,000 for Greece and €2,114 for Romania. For Greece, the amount has been paid in full, and for Romania, €206,000 had been paid, while the remaining €1,908 will be paid at a later date
verifier_note: I downloaded the iXBRL zip from ATHEX and found the text verbatim, including the goodwill table (price 9,498/2,114; net assets 2,730/2,064; goodwill 6,768/50) and the +517/-574 results. CORRECTION: the scraper says the price was net assets plus a modest premium. That holds for Romania only; Greece carried a 3.5x premium, probably for footlocker.gr and the flagship Ermou site. Baseline BL08 has only the FL-side total ($12M net of $1M cash, $6M receivable, $6M gain). CONFLICT: FL booked a $6M receivable, but Fourlis shows only EUR 1.9M deferred, so the difference may be cash/working-capital or FX terms. Downgraded A to B because this adds detail to a pre-deal transaction already in the baseline.

claim: Fourlis' FL licensee store count went from 10 (30-Jun-25) to 13 (31-Dec-25) to 18 (30-Jun-26: Greece 10, Bulgaria 4, Romania 4). Five more are scheduled for H2-26: Kallithea (Jul), Nea Erythraia (Sep), Tsimiski in Thessaloniki (Oct), Kavala (Oct) and Plovdiv (Sep), which would make about 23. All of these are greenfield openings. Romania has stayed at 4 stores since 2025. No stores have opened yet in Cyprus, Croatia, Slovenia, Bosnia or Montenegro. Capex was EUR 2.0M for the 4 new Greek stores (about EUR 0.5M each) and EUR 0.4M for Ring Mall Sofia. New FL leases added EUR 7M of right-of-use assets. The sports segment's H1-26 EBIT was -EUR 0.65M and its PBT -EUR 4.85M.
data_point: Licensee FL stores: 10, then 13, then 18, about 23 planned by Oct-26. About EUR 0.5M capex per store. Sports segment H1-26 PBT -EUR 4.848M (vs -EUR 1.601M a year earlier).
original_quote: As of 30 June 2026, the segment operated 10 FOOT LOCKER stores in Greece, having added four new stores during the period, namely in Patras (30/4/2026), Volos (5/6/2026), Glyfada and Lamia (19/6/2026).
verifier_note: I extracted the PDF text and verified the store counts, dates, H2 pipeline, EUR 2M/0.4M capex, EUR 7M new FL leases and segment EBIT/PBT. The FY25 report confirms 13 stores at 31-Dec-25 (GR 6, BG 3, RO 4; Romanian stores taken over 14-Apr-2025 plus Iasi opened 23-Jun-2025). Partial overlap: A_w1_buyers already has '7 new FL stores in 2026' and segment EBIT -0.7M. What is new here is the store-by-store series, the stalled Romanian count, the unused territories and the capex per store. Downgraded A to B because the item is context for the licensing route, not direct DKS-owned evidence.

claim: Breaking down the rise in DKS's licensed store count (246 at close to 266 at 8/1/26) by partner: since close, the 10-Q tables show 34 licensed openings and 14 closures (Q3 FY25 +8/-4; Q4 FY25 +8/-4; Q1 FY26 +5/-3; Q2 FY26 +13/-3). Fourlis' greenfield openings explain about 8-9 of the openings, with 0 closures; Metro Brands India explains about 1-2. The remaining ~24 openings and all ~14 closures sit with Middle East and SE-Asian partners. No owned FL market has moved to a licensee since 8-Sep-2025: the Greece/Romania conversion closed 14-Apr-2025, before the deal.
data_point: +34/-14 gross licensed flows since close. About 25% of openings are European (all Fourlis greenfield). 0 owned-to-licensed conversions.
source_name: Own computation: DKS FY25 10-K/Q1-Q2 FY26 10-Q store tables (WORKING_NOTES W01/W04) plus Fourlis FY25/H1-26 and Metro Brands filings
verifier_note: I checked the arithmetic against W04/W05 store tables: 246+8-4=250; FY25 stub +16/-8 to 254; FY26 YTD +18/-6 to 266, which implies Q2 +13/-3. The reclassification column is blank (—) in every table, which supports the claim that no owned-to-licensed transfers have happened. Fourlis counts were verified (10 to 13 to 18, plus Kallithea in Jul-26). The exact dates of Fourlis' H2-25 openings (Halandri 27-Nov-25 is confirmed post-close; Larissa and Heraklion were not dated) and Metro's split around 8-Sep-25 are not pinned down, hence 'about'. The Middle East/SE Asia residual is inferred, not observed. Tier B because this is a computation.

claim: Store-locator census (2026-10-07): Alshaya lists 40 Foot Locker locations in 7 Middle East countries (BH 1, JO 2, KW 10, OM 1, QA 5, SA 12, AE 9). Fourlis has about 18-19 and Metro India about 7. That puts Europe at roughly 7% of DKS's 266 licensed stores, and Fourlis' SE-Europe territory is the only European licence found. By subtraction, about 200 licensed stores sit with MAP Active and any undisclosed partners.
data_point: Alshaya 40; Fourlis about 19; Metro about 7; residual about 200 (inferred)
source_name: Alshaya store locator; Fourlis H1-26 report; MAP Active H1-26 FS
verifier_note: I re-pulled all 7 country pages (HTTP 200): 1/2/10/1/5/12/9 = 40, matching the scraper. Aventura Mall did not appear in the Kuwait page HTML. The roughly 200 attributed to MAP Active is a residual, not an observation. It conflicts with E_w1_apac-asia (bazaar.town says Alshaya runs 'over 70' FL stores) and with FL's 2023 Investor Day target of about 130 licensed stores in Asia by 2026, so the locator may undercount Alshaya. Mixing dates (266 at 8/1/26 vs locator at 10/7) adds noise. Downgraded A to C: the Europe-share point stands, but the partner split is uncertain.

claim: Fourlis' CEO is publicly enthusiastic about the licence. In Dec-2025 Vasilakos called Foot Locker 'a much easier concept with better profitability' and said he would ideally open 15 new FL stores in 2026, but that suitable prime sites are hard to find; by Apr-May 2026 the guidance was 10-12. FL's first 'Home Court' space in Europe launched in the licensee's relaunched Ermou, Athens store (Reimagined Evolution, Apr-2026). The 10-year target is 100+ FL stores and more than EUR 250M of revenue.
data_point: 2026 ambition of 15 new FL stores cut to 10-12 because of site scarcity. First European Home Court opened in a licensed store. 10-year target 100+ stores and >EUR 250M revenue.
original_quote: Footlocker που είναι ένα concept πολύ ευκολότερο με καλύτερη κερδοφορία και πάει δυνατά στις χώρες
english_translation: Footlocker, which is a much easier concept with better profitability and is going strong in the countries.
verifier_note: All three pages were fetched directly (HTTP 200) and the quotes found verbatim: BusinessDaily datePublished 2025-12-10; Capital.gr 2025-12-10 ('Ιδανικά θα θέλαμε 15 νέα Foot Locker ... δεν είναι εύκολο να βρεθούν τα κατάλληλα ακίνητα', with 7-8 in Greece); Insider.gr 2026-04-09 (Home Court 'για πρώτη φορά στην Ευρώπη' at Ermou; up to 12 openings in 2026; 100+ stores, >EUR 250M in 10 years). DUPLICATE parts dropped: the 6-7% year-1 margin and 10-12 openings (B_w1_registry-nordics-cee, D_w1_sector-backdrop). Downgraded B to C: this is incremental evidence of licensee appetite, which is upbeat CEO talk, while segment PBT is negative.

claim: Foot Locker's European LinkedIn postings show no licensing, franchise or partner-development roles. They do show a wave of Dutch store-manager postings dated 20 Sep-1 Oct 2026 (Amersfoort, Amsterdam, Arnhem, Breda, Eindhoven, Groningen, Heerlen, Hilversum, Utrecht x2, Den Bosch). A new Utrecht EMEA role, Manager Internal Communications & Employer Branding (posted 3-Oct-2026), lists 'restructures' among the major moments it will handle communications for.
data_point: About 112 FL Europe postings re-pulled: 0 licensing/franchise roles; about 11-13 NL store-manager postings in about 10 days; comms role names 'restructures'
original_quote: Define and own the EMEA internal communications plan, aligned to business priorities, brand voice, and major moments (restructures, leadership changes, GTM launches)
verifier_note: I re-pulled the LinkedIn guest search on 2026-10-07 and got 112 unique FL postings in NL/IT/EU, with none for licensing, franchise or partners. I found 11 NL store-manager postings (some requests failed with SSL errors; the scraper found 13). The Lease Admin and comms quotes were verified on the posting pages. Mostly DUPLICATE of other confirmed items: the careers-API census (A_w1_company-side-new), Utrecht HQ temp roles and Lease Admin wording (C_w1_labor-rest), the Italy store requisitions (C_w1_news-italy) and EU store-manager postings (D_w1_chatter). Only three elements are new: no licensing roles, the Dutch store-manager wave, and the 'restructures' wording. Downgraded A to C: these are weak, ambiguous signals.
